//: Handbook §26 delivery gate, point 3: numeric floors for mobile performance and accessibility. A threshold with no job that runs it produces the same software as no threshold, so these are merge conditions rather than aspirations.
//measured: Set 2026-08-12 from the median of three CI runs, not guessed: performance 64, accessibility 97, best-practices 100, SEO 100, LCP 6.8s, CLS 0, TBT 10ms.
//headroom: Each floor sits below its measured score by roughly the run-to-run variance Lighthouse shows on a shared runner. A floor set flush against today's number goes red on noise, and a gate that cries wolf is a gate somebody removes - the failure this whole adoption is written against. Raise them as the scores improve: the ratchet idea applied to a number instead of a count.
//on-performance: 0.55 against a measured 64 is the loosest floor here, deliberately. LCP is 6.8s and the largest remaining cause is the render-blocking Google Fonts stylesheet on a third-party origin - DEBT-04, which is also a privacy finding, so the same commit fixes both. Tighten this to 0.75 when it lands.
//on-layout-shift: Measured 0 after width/height landed on all 27 images. Asserted at 0.1 to lock it in: it is the one metric here that is currently perfect and the easiest to lose by accident.
//on-blocking-time: Measured 10ms. 500 is generous on purpose - the point is catching a script that starts blocking the main thread, not policing normal variation.
//on-lcp: Warning rather than error, and this is the honest place for it. At 6.8s it fails any floor worth setting, so asserting on it would make the gate permanently red - the exact failure the ratchet prevents everywhere else here. It warns so the number stays in view, and it becomes an error when DEBT-04 removes the render-blocking third-party stylesheet.
//no-comments-below: Every key inside `assertions` is read by LHCI as an AUDIT NAME. A `//` comment there is asserted as an audit that does not exist and fails with 'auditRan'. That happened here on 2026-08-12; the commentary lives at this level instead, where LHCI does not look.
